title: Aiptasia Spawning and Embryo/Larvae Handling
author: Pringle Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ru2d6ye

steps.title: Collect pedal lacerates
steps.instruction: Collect 30–40 pedal lacerates from the chosen Aiptasia strain and place them into a medium tank containing 500 mL artificial seawater (ASW).

steps.title: Transfer small anemones to tank
steps.instruction: Move fully developed small anemones into a large tank with 1.5 L ASW; this tank is designated the “tiny polyp” tank.

steps.title: Maintain and grow animals
steps.instruction: Keep all tanks at room temperature (22–27 °C) under cool‑white light (~25 µmol photons · m⁻² · s⁻¹). Feed anemones twice weekly, perform water changes several hours later, swipe tank sides with lint‑free Kimwipes, and remove pedal lacerates with clean disposable spatulas. Growth from a lacerate to spawning size typically requires 3–5 months.

substeps.instruction: Polyps 1–3 mm pedal disc → new large tank with 1.5 L ASW ("small polyps" tank).
Polyps 3–5 mm pedal disc → new large tank with 1.5 L ASW ("medium polyps" tank).
Anemones 5–6 mm pedal disc → medium tank with 500 mL ASW, max 10 animals per tank ("large polyps" tank).

steps.title: Prepare spawning tanks
steps.instruction: When polyps in the "large polyp" tank exceed 8 mm pedal disc diameter, transfer three animals of the same strain and sex into a small tank containing 200 mL ASW; this tank will later be placed in a spawning incubator.

steps.title: Configure spawning incubators
steps.instruction: Set incubators to 29 °C with an inverted 12 h light : 12 h dark cycle (light 4 PM–4 AM, dark 4 AM–4 PM) at ~25 µmol photons · m⁻² · s⁻¹ (cool‑white fluorescent). Simulate a 28‑day lunar cycle: first 5 nights blue LED light (~450 nm) at 10 µmol · m⁻² · s⁻¹, followed by 23 dark nights. House ~12 tanks per incubator, each with 3 anemones; keep sexes separate (e.g., 5 male tanks, 8 female tanks) unless mixed‑sex cultures are acceptable.

steps.title: Acclimate tanks to incubator
steps.instruction: Place the spawning tanks prepared in step 5 into a spawning incubator seven days before the simulated full‑moon begins; each tank remains for three lunar cycles before being replaced.

steps.title: Feed and clean spawning tanks
steps.instruction: Feed all spawning tanks at least four times per week with live brine shrimp in the morning. In the afternoon, after the onset of “daylight” in the incubator, change the water and clean the tanks; replace any tank that becomes excessively dirty.

steps.title: Monitor spawning events
steps.instruction: Check for spawning in the dark using a red light 5–6 h after the start of the dark phase. Spawning usually occurs 10–13 days after the end of the full‑moon phase (often between 9–10 AM, 5–6 h after darkness onset). Record egg and sperm appearance as described.

steps.title: Concentrate sperm‑containing water
steps.instruction: Collect sperm‑containing water and centrifuge 50 mL at ~3700 × g for 15 min; discard most supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 0.5–2 mL ASW. If higher concentration is needed, perform a second centrifugation of the resuspended volume in a microcentrifuge tube at ~4000 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Filter sperm water
steps.instruction: Pass the concentrated sperm suspension through two stacked sieves (120 µm mesh followed by 20 µm mesh) to remove debris, and collect the filtered sperm in a glass beaker of at least 250 mL capacity.

steps.title: Handle collected eggs
steps.instruction: If eggs have settled on the tank bottom, transfer them with a disposable polypropylene pipette into a 250 mL glass dish (4.5 in diameter) and dilute with ASW. If eggs are floating, decant the egg‑containing water into two 250 mL glass dishes. Do not use polystyrene containers, as they damage unfertilized eggs.

steps.title: Fertilize eggs with sperm
steps.instruction: Add 10–15 mL of the filtered sperm suspension to 100 mL of eggs, then distribute the fertilized mixture into 60 × 15 mm glass petri dishes. Avoid polystyrene vessels, which reduce fertilization success.

steps.title: Observe embryo development
steps.instruction: At room temperature, the 4‑cell stage should appear 1–3 h after fertilization (slower at lower temperatures). Ciliated blastulae become visible 6–8 h post‑fertilization, and planula larvae develop by the following day.
